title: Degree of a line-bundle homomorphism from its top intersection
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $A/k$ an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] of dimension $g\geq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For any invertible sheaf $N$ on $A$ [def-sc-invertible-module], let $\phi_N:A\to A^\vee$ be the homomorphism of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]. For any group-scheme homomorphism $h:A\to A^\vee$ [def-sc-group-scheme] define $d(h)$ to be its degree if it is an isogeny [def-sc-isogeny], and zero otherwise; the degree of an isogeny is the dimension over $k$ of the coordinate algebra of its finite scheme-theoretic kernel. Then
$$d(\phi_N)=\left(\frac{(N^g\cdot A)}{g!}\right)^2\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q,$$
where the intersection number is [def-sc-intersection-number]. No ampleness or nondegeneracy of $N$ is assumed.

source.place: Chapter I, Theorem 11.1(a),(b), printed p.54, with the zero-degree convention for non-isogenies preceding Theorem 10.9, printed p.46. Combine the degree/Euler-characteristic square formula with abelian Riemann–Roch; the identity applies to arbitrary invertible sheaves.

proof.text: Put $c=\chi(A,N)$. Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-euler-tensor-homogeneity] to the given $A,N$: for every integer $m$, $\chi(A,N^{\otimes m})=m^gc$. Consequently, for integers $n_1,\ldots,n_g$, tensoring powers of the same invertible sheaf gives $\chi(A,N^{\otimes n_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes N^{\otimes n_g})=c(n_1+\cdots+n_g)^g$. The input requires exactly algebraic closedness, an abelian variety of positive dimension, and invertibility, all assumed here; it does not require ampleness.

source.place: Chapter I, Theorem 11.1(b), printed p.54; homogeneous Euler-polynomial consequence

proof.text: Use [def-sc-intersection-number] with $X=Z=A$, the identity closed immersion and $\mathcal L_j=N$ for every $j$. The polynomial defining $(N^g\cdot A)$ is therefore $c(n_1+\cdots+n_g)^g$. Equality of its integer values determines the polynomial over $\mathbf Q$: fixing all but one variable gives infinitely many roots of the difference, and repeating in each variable makes every coefficient vanish. The coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_g$ is $c\,g!$, since each of the $g$ factors must contribute a different variable and there are $g!$ permutations. Thus $(N^g\cdot A)=g!c$. Since $g!$ is nonzero in $\mathbf Q$, $c=(N^g\cdot A)/g!$.

source.place: Tag 0BEP, definition-intersection-number; coefficient calculation after the homogeneous Euler identity

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-euler-degree-square] to $A,N$. Its homomorphism is the same $\phi_N$ and its degree uses the same scheme-theoretic kernel length, with value zero when the homomorphism is not an isogeny. It gives $d(\phi_N)=c^2$. In particular this step covers a positive-dimensional kernel; no assumption that $\phi_N$ is an isogeny has entered.

source.place: Chapter I, Theorem 11.1(a), printed p.54; degree-zero convention at printed p.46

proof.text: Embed the integer equality of step 3 into $\mathbf Q$ and substitute $c=(N^g\cdot A)/g!$ from step 2. This gives $d(\phi_N)=((N^g\cdot A)/g!)^2$, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q50-2cb12de90 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Milne AV Theorem 11.1(a),(b) (printed p.54, PDF p.60) and the zero-degree convention before Theorem 10.9 (printed p.46). The item statement is unchanged and is faithful to them: arbitrary invertible N, g>=1, degree = kernel length (def-sc-isogeny's order of the kernel = dim_k Gamma), and 0 for a non-isogeny. Step 1 cites the tensor-homogeneity node with exactly the same hypotheses, and the extension to signed tensor powers is elementary. Step 2 is correctly marked elementary: with X=Z=A and i=id in def-sc-intersection-number (Tag 0BEP), the polynomial equals c(sum n_i)^g on Z^g, so the coefficient of n_1...n_g is g!c, divided in Q. Step 3 cites the degree-square node, which uses the same phi_N from polarization-calculus and the same zero convention. Step 4 is substitution in Q. Both new nodes are self-contained, statement-only and true, and neither restates the item. Degree-square is Milne 11.1(a), and it vanishes on positive-dimensional K(L) by Mumford's vanishing theorem. Homogeneity follows from Riemann-Roch and (nD)^g=n^g D^g, and at n=0 it agrees with chi(O_A)=0. I tested both on O_A, an elliptic curve with any degree, a pullback to E x E, and L^{-1}. A statement scan of the whole DAG for abelian-variety nodes mentioning chi, degree or Riemann-Roch found no duplicate; Hilbert/Snapper polynomiality and lem-sc-isogeny-degree are different results. Batch-5 flag: the new node cites lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus only to construct A^vee and phi_L. That is a general abelian-variety construction, not given by the trace formula or Poincare duality and not a step of their proofs, and the item already cited the same node on the base for the same phi_N, so it is outside the assumptions. No tool_uses, no SGA, no cycle. blueprint.from.node is null, inherited from the base item. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem IsAbelianVariety.line_bundle_degree_square {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (A : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj A] [IsAbelianVariety A] (g : ℕ) (_hg : 1 ≤ g) (hA : topologicalKrullDim A.left = ((g : ℕ∞) : WithBot ℕ∞)) (D : AbelianDualPoincareDatum A) (N : A.left.Modules) [N.IsInvertible] (φ : A ⟶ D.dual) [IsMonHom φ] (_hφ : ClassifiesAbelianDifference D N φ) : @ite ℚ (IsIsogeny φ) (Classical.propDecidable _) (isogenyDegree φ : ℚ) 0 = (@Scheme.Modules.selfIntersectionNumber k _ A.left ⟨A.hom⟩ (inferInstance : IsProper A.hom) A.left inferInstance (𝟙 A.left) inferInstance g hA N inferInstance / (Nat.factorial g : ℚ)) ^ 2

No ampleness or isogeny assumption, no universe restriction.
